name: LdapRelayScan – check domain controllers for LDAP signing and LDAPS channel binding enforcement
what: A small Python tool that tells you whether domain controllers enforce the two server-side protections against NTLM relay to LDAP: LDAPS channel binding (Never / When supported / Always, determined unauthenticated from the bind error) and LDAP server signing (requires a valid domain credential, detected from the strongerAuthRequired result). It works from error-based enumeration, so it reads the effective state of each DC rather than what a GPO report claims.
when: As the verification step after you set 'Domain controller: LDAP server signing requirements' and LdapEnforceChannelBinding, as a per-DC drift check (one DC missing the GPO is enough for a relay path), and in purple-team engagements before you try any relay to LDAP. It complements the NTLM-layer signing rollout (KB5135557): NTLM signing, LDAP signing and LDAPS channel binding are separate controls.
cost_note: Repository last updated November 2024; review the code and dependencies (msldap) before running it in production networks.
example: Install in an isolated venv or the provided Docker image: `python3 -m pip install -r requirements_exact.txt`, or `docker build -f docker/Dockerfile -t ldaprelayscan .`.
Channel binding only, unauthenticated: `python3 LdapRelayScan.py -method LDAPS -dc-ip <dc-ip>`.
Signing and channel binding with a low-privilege test account: `python3 LdapRelayScan.py -method BOTH -dc-ip <dc-ip> -u <testuser> -p <password>`.
Run it against every DC, not just the one DNS returns first, and keep the output as evidence next to the GPO change.
pitfalls: DNS must resolve the domain properly from where you run it; on a non-domain-joined host or through SOCKS, fix resolution first or results are misleading.
The BOTH method performs real authenticated binds: use a dedicated test account, not a personal or admin credential, and expect the binds in DC logs.
'When supported' channel binding still lets clients that do not send a CBT through; only 'Always' closes LDAPS relay.
Error-based detection depends on DC behaviour the author observed; re-validate against the DC's actual configuration after major Windows Server upgrades.
